entries.summary: Weekend reassessment: November 20 close still anchors a bearish elevated-downside outlook for Nov 23–25. Reuters Nasdaq -5.28%, rounded SOX -11%, VIX ~37, 10Y ~4.93%; secondary QQQ -5.67%, NVDA -14.01%. No new US cash session, independently verified synchronized new prices or newly curated Open Watch event. The scheduled Tuesday AI hardware earnings and Wednesday inflation/growth data remain key catalysts. No incremental material change.

editorial.marketOverview: The U.S. cash market is closed for the weekend following Friday's severe technology selloff. Reuters reported Nasdaq -5.28% and semiconductor stocks about -11%; a secondary closing report placed QQQ at -5.67% and Nvidia at -14.01%. These are Friday observations, not Saturday quotes. Friday's broad market and international technology declines establish the existing risk-off context.
editorial.whatChanged: Since the prior 21:17 ET assessment there has been no new regular-session trading and no newly curated Open Watch catalyst. Fresh review of Reuters' week-ahead coverage and the company earnings calendar adds no independent material change in the expected three-day path. The baseline remains bearish rather than extrapolating a fresh decline from repeated Friday headlines.
editorial.marketInterpretation: Semiconductor underperformance, approximate four-to-one negative breadth and elevated volatility support persistent risk aversion. Reuters' 10Y near 4.93% lacks a synchronized 2Y observation, so no current yield curve is asserted; the older 4.94%-4.65% pair implies +29 basis points. Direct FedWatch probabilities and contract-matched oil are unavailable. Expected AI-earnings or macro impacts are scenarios, not observed responses.
editorial.threeDayPath: Monday November 23 can produce either renewed selling or a violent oversold bounce; the bearish baseline remains until joint QQQ/SOX stabilization is corroborated by breadth and volatility. Tuesday November 24 brings Dell and Analog Devices earnings and a test of AI hardware demand sentiment. Wednesday November 25 concentrates U.S. macro releases and Fed Beige Book risk, potentially changing rate expectations. No price targets are warranted without fresh synchronized observations.
editorial.bullCase: Extreme selling and lower Treasury yields may allow short covering, but a durable bullish case needs QQQ and SOX/SMH strengthening together, broadening advances and VIX/VXN falling over Monday and Tuesday. The mere absence of weekend news is not a bullish catalyst.
editorial.bearCase: Friday's Nasdaq -5.28%, rounded SOX -11%, QQQ -5.67% and steep Nvidia decline suggest forced risk reduction and vulnerable AI leadership. Weak Tuesday AI-hardware results or hawkish Wednesday macro repricing could extend the selloff, but those outcomes are not yet known.
editorial.watchNext: At Monday's open obtain fresh synchronized QQQ, SOX/SMH, VXN/VIX, breadth and 10Y/2Y observations. Confirm CME FedWatch and matched oil contracts. Track Monday HPE/Zoom, Tuesday Analog Devices/Dell/HP/Best Buy and Wednesday macro releases; monitor Open Watch for genuinely new curated events.
